name: Build Integration
desc: Integrate a source system that has NO built-in connector: author a secret-free DATA manifest, test it live read-only from your shell, confirm the canonical mapping, register it, then scan + capture behavior — never handling credentials.
body:
Use this during the Source stage when you must integrate an existing system (CRM/ERP/BPM/database/API) that the app has NO built-in connector for. You author the connector as a secret-free DATA manifest and test it live, all from your shell. You NEVER handle credentials. THE LOOP: probe → draft manifest → validate → try → confirm the canonical mapping → register → scan + capture behavior → write a findings skill. AUTH HANDSHAKE (secret-free). You never see tokens. The app brokers the connection (OAuth / OS keychain) and you reference it only by a HANDLE — `--project --source `. The CLI resolves the secret itself. Never put a credential in a command, a manifest, or a findings note. THE COMMANDS (run them exactly). - `bsc data connector probe --base-url [--openapi ] [--path

] [--project --source ]` — fetch a sample response or parse an OpenAPI doc; emits a DRAFT `RuntimePreset` (resources + `array_key` guesses) for you to refine. Read-only. - `bsc data connector validate` — pipe the manifest JSON on stdin; checks it is well-formed, secret-free, and uses a sanctioned auth method. Run this before every `try`. - `bsc data connector try --project --source ` — pipe the manifest; a SAMPLE-READS-ONLY dry run against the live source (≤12 objects × ≤20 rows). Returns the discovered shape and PERSISTS NOTHING. Iterate the manifest against this until the shape is right. - `bsc data connector map` — pipe a `try` result; emits a STARTER canonical `DataModel` for you to refine into the project's vendor-neutral schema. - `bsc data connector add` — pipe the validated manifest to REGISTER it. Reusable thereafter. - `bsc data scan ...` — materialize the canonical Data Model into the project store (this is the real, persisted read). THE MANIFEST (`RuntimePreset`) — secret-free DATA, never code: { "id": "", "label": "", "category": "crm|erp|…", "base_url": "https://…", "auth": "oauth|token|apikey|basic", "resources": [ { "name": "accounts", "path": "accounts", "array_key": "data" } ] } `base_url` is the API root; `auth` names the sanctioned method (the app holds the actual secret); each `resources` entry maps one source object to a canonical name, its request `path`, and the `array_key` the row array sits under in the response. NEVER put a credential in the manifest — secrets live in the keychain; you pass a handle. BEHAVIOR CAPTURE (you do this — there are NO native behavior scanners). Probe the source's metadata/admin endpoints (e.g. the Salesforce Tooling API, OData `$metadata`, or the OpenAPI doc), reason over that metadata, and author the vendor-neutral Platform Behavior Summary via `bsc data scan set` — pipe a `PlatformScan` JSON with `automations`, `business_processes`, and `derived_logic`. This is how automations, business processes, and derived logic become migratable alongside the data. CAPTURE FINDINGS AS A REUSABLE SKILL (do this on success). After a connector works, write a per-integration findings skill so the knowledge persists for the next session: echo '{"name":" integration findings","kind":"workflow","desc":"…","prompt":"resources + array_keys, canonical mapping, auth method, behavior endpoints…","tools":["read_file"]}' | bsc skill add --group "$BSC_SESSION_SKILL_GROUP" It prints the new skill id. Record the resources + their `array_key`s, the canonical mapping, the auth method, and the metadata/behavior endpoints you used — enough that the next integration of the same system starts from a working manifest.
